concept: Rating is a short row of five marks printed as round dot lattices, the way a panel prints a scale of levels. A lit mark is a solid disc of dots and an empty mark is a hollow ring of dots, so the number is read from the shape alone. In display mode it only shows a value, half marks included; in pick mode it is a radio group that the arrow keys walk.

default_to_avoid.pattern: row of five yellow stars, filled yellow against outlined grey, with a hover preview
default_to_avoid.why_not: A star spends a hue on a score, which P1 forbids, and the empty star is told from the filled one by colour first. Rating tells them by shape, a solid lattice against a hollow ring, in ink only.

default_to_avoid.pattern: rating built from clickable icons with no group, no value and no keyboard map
default_to_avoid.why_not: Five unrelated buttons name no group and expose no value. Rating is one radio group with a printed name, a visible value and arrow, Home and End keys.

references.source: Braun LE 1 loudspeaker grille (Dieter Rams, 1959): a field of round holes where the lit and the unlit are told by pattern
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a printed scale of marks beside the dial, read by position
apps/lab/rating/index.html: round lattice, square block, diamonds in a window

derivation.consequence: a lit level uses ink at full step
derivation.form: A lit mark prints its dots in text.primary and an empty mark prints in text.secondary, never orange, and the shape (disc against ring) carries the difference as well.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: A mark draws its lattice at control.check, 24px, inside a control.md square that is the whole target, so five marks stand 220px wide.

derivation.consequence: arrows step a detent, Home and End reach the ends
derivation.form: The marks are native radios sharing one name, so the arrows walk and choose, Home picks 1 and End picks the last, and only one mark is a tab stop.

derivation.consequence: a grille that shows a value exposes it as text to assistive tech
derivation.form: Display mode is role img named with the value as words, and pick mode prints the value beside the marks as tabular text.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: The chosen value is marked by the lattice shape and ink, so the selection never uses the orange.

options.name: round lattice, lit disc against hollow ring
square block against four corner marks

variants.reason: A reads at once as lit against empty with no colour, and its half mark is a disc on one side and a ring on the other; B has too few dots left in its empty mark to read as a mark at all, and C puts a control inside a recessed window, which is the form of a display, so it reads as read-only.

root.why: A column holding the printed name above the row of marks, so the label and the marks share one left edge.

legend.why: The group's printed name in the label size and secondary ink, set on the inset line above the marks like the legend of Radio.

row.why: The marks and the value sit on one line with no gap between targets, so the row is a continuous 44px band to hit.

mark.why: One choice, a 44px square target that centres a 24px lattice, so a small drawing never makes a small target.

input.why: The native radio is visually hidden and stays focusable and announced, so the arrow keys and the form value come from the browser.

glyph.why: A 5 by 5 field of round holes at the Grille pitch; the ring holes are always printed and the core holes are lit by the value.

dot.why: One round hole of the lattice; a core hole fades in when its mark is lit and sinks back when it is not, as the Icon dots do.

value.why: The value printed after the marks in tabular figures, so the number can be read as well as the shape and does not shift as it changes.

data-fill=full.why: A fully lit mark prints its core dots and uses primary ink, so lit differs from empty by shape and by ink step.

data-fill=half.why: A half mark lights the core dots of the inline-start half only, for display values like 3.5, and mirrors in right-to-left.

data-fill=empty.why: An empty mark keeps only its ring of dots in secondary ink, a hollow shape that is measurably different from the solid lattice.

hover.why: Hover only darkens an empty mark's ink one step, because a real key does not rise when a hand approaches it.

active.why: Pressing moves the lattice down by the press travel on motion.press, the same small drop every key makes, and returns on release.

focus-visible.why: The focused mark draws the shared focus ring around its 44px target so the keyboard position is always visible.

data-disabled.why: A disabled rating drops to the disabled opacity, loses its press travel and shows a not-allowed cursor.

data-readonly.why: Display mode draws the lattice at the small icon size with no target, no hover and no cursor, since nothing in it can be pressed.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion the dots only fade, with no size change and no press travel.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the lattice draws in the text colour and the unlit core dots stay hidden, so the shapes survive.

data-on.why: A lit dot is drawn at full size and full ink; an unlit core dot stays in its hole at the dot scale and invisible, so each hole is lit or not.

opacity.why: Core dots fade in on motion.release and out on motion.exit, the way a grille fills hole by hole, with none of it under Reduce motion.

transform.why: Core dots scale up on motion.release and sink on motion.exit, and the whole lattice drops by the press travel on motion.press, as any key does.
